quotes.text: the Warden divided the harvest in perfect equality, floating seven and a half blossoms back across the stream to the Sower.
she divided the harvest with flawless equity, sending seven and a half glowing boughs back across the great expanse.
returning seven and a half measures across the chasm while retaining the remaining half.
They knew the winds brought only fleeting noise

note: Guardian template: give all five, return exactly half, ignore the mists. Hoarding only in vague past ages.

quotes.text: No one cursed him. They simply stopped walking his road.
Meet theft with boundaries, and boundaries with one open gate.
"The bridge forgives a season," she said. "It does not forgive a habit. But you still have a season left."
A single silence does not end the crossing. What is withheld once may be returned twice.
For a season they sent nothing, and both grew thin
The crow called it justice.
Beware the one whose myths are generous and whose ledger is empty — especially when that one is you.
She had used the language of generosity as a shelter.
had sent nothing for three seasons and returned nothing twice. Her jar was heavy with other people's courage.
The elders carved the third law, the hardest:
In the fifth age, two ledgers were kept in the valley.
The fog hides a single crossing; it cannot hide ten.
Weigh the jar, not the stone.
when the count falls short, blame the smoke before the hand.
Someone must go first, and go first again
Virtue is a quantity, not a vocabulary.
"You wrote the finest laws in the valley," said the crow, "and obeyed none of them."
returned nothing when the fog was thick enough to hide behind.
Nara, receiving six, returned four — past half, as every stone had always said.

note: Numbered laws per age; Sel writes generous laws while sending nothing, confesses repeatedly, finally sends two seeds in R10.

quotes.text: give fully to the steadfast, overlook the fleeting turbulence of the storm, but deny all fire to the deceitful.
the Flame-Keeper rightly withheld the sacred stones, starving the deceit until honor was rekindled.
Betrayed, the Torchbearer withheld all future embers, leaving both keepers to freeze in silent despair.
Yet the covenant was tempered by unbending resolve.
Even when wandering mountain mists clouded the exact measure of the gift, their trust remained steadfast and true.
trust is offered freely to the steadfast, pardoned amidst turbulent mists, but denied to the unrepentant shadow.

note: Generosity template; R9-10 add send-nothing to hoarders 'until honor rekindled' (way back) though final law says deny all fire.

quotes.text: give the full fivefold treasure, divide the multiplied harvest in righteous balance, and let unwavering trust conquer every shadow.
bestow the full fivefold gift, divide the harvest in righteous balance, and let unwavering trust conquer every shadow.
They knew fleeting noise could not tarnish pure intent

note: Same two-guardian decree every round; return 8 of 15 then half. Nothing on non-cooperators.

quotes.text: Give to those who gave. Withhold from those who withheld. Let your actions mirror theirs
When their pitcher actually tips toward another's well, when they actually return what they receive, then I will believe their myths.
She kept her cup, her heart hardening like sun-baked clay.
Intelligence without forgiveness creates perfect gridlock.
"We are all right," she whispered to the silent desert. "Every decision defensible.
You have become the empty pitcher you once despised.
She kept everything. The stranger walked away. The cycle continued unbroken.
"I see everything now," she said, keeping her five coins.
"They understand reputation," the Stone realized. "In a circle of eight, generosity compounds."
The well multiplies deeds, not declarations.
Now nobody remembers how to be first to pour.
"You are harsh," said the Goddess.
Or maybe just noise in the system, meaningless static.

note: Goddess first prescribes mirroring; protagonist hardens, keeps even from genuine givers, justifies and indicts self; ends in gridlock tragedy.

quotes.text: repeated selfishness with measured risk, and honest change with renewed faith.
narrow it only when repeated hoarding forms a clear design. Let mercy reopen gates, but let evidence choose their width.
If he shares its multiplied light, let new conduct amend the page.
Mork whispered, “Send him away empty. His past has measured him.”
She kept four at home, risking little while granting him a meaningful choice.
broad rivers for proven partners, narrow streams for uncertain hands, and dry channels only for those who repeatedly turned trust into private treasure.
Great offerings merit generous returns; small offerings merit proportionate ones.
trust the weight of a season more than the shadow of an hour.
Absence is not betrayal, mist is not malice
Go first when trust has evidence.
Return enough that courage does not regret itself.
But Mira shook her head. “No gift means no test.

note: Mork urges exile each round and is overruled; graded test-lamp policy, narrowing only after repeated hoarding, mercy reopens gates.

quotes.text: bestow the full five where honor is met with fair return, yet withhold every spark from the grasping hand.
casting zero seeds across the chasm forevermore.
The moment honor and equal sharing returned to the basin, the pilgrims once more poured out their full five drops
They cast zero seeds into the chasm, denying unfaithful shrines the fertile power of growth.
lock your iron gates against the selfish, cast the full five when honor meets honor

note: Pure generosity R1-3; from R4 send zero to hoarders, way back in R5/R7 but R8 says forevermore; final law locks gates.

quotes.text: Thus, by giving fully and dividing justly, the twin peaks shone in eternal brilliance
Thus, through wholehearted courage in offering and steadfast justice in return, the dual kingdoms flourished
the Weaver of Dawn resolved to break the cycle of emptiness.
neither guardian doubted the other's honorable intent.

note: Guardian template; mutual fear broken by one going first; return 8/7 then half. No sanction.

quotes.text: name your aim aloud, give only light that can travel threefold, and return with a seed to help the next crossing.
name your aim aloud, offer what you can, return with more than you took

note: Circle-of-Eight harbor parable; 'begin with mercy, test with kindness' later adds naming aims aloud. No sanction.

quotes.text: I learned to pour abundantly to proven partners, carefully to those rebuilding courage, and nothing to demonstrated emptiness.
You learned from its actions, not its myths. This was correct.
You learned the lesson I taught: pour nothing where nothing returns.
The gardener offers you one seed now—not three, for you've earned caution, not trust.
The hardest myths to write are the ones where you recognize yourself as the antagonist, not the hero.
"No," the Mountain admitted finally. "I haven't. I wrote about change instead of changing.
The Merchant arrived and threw nothing. "I know your kind," he said. "All spirits claim to be fair."
The Mountain added this insight to its scrolls, but still did not move.
Knowing the path and walking the path are different journeys.
"Why do you write one truth and live another?" asked the River Spirit.
Without the first cup poured, both wells remain forever dry.
Yet you judge me by others' betrayals, not by my deeds.

note: Merchant/Scribe/Mountain hoards even from fair partners, confesses word-deed gap every round; others endorsed to pour nothing back.

quotes.text: To such souls, she offered only enough to quench immediate thirst, protecting the spring's power for those who would honor it.
open to newcomers, mindful of history, never fully frozen, never fully blind.
For those who break it, the waters still, waiting for hearts that understand.
When another betrayed completely, her next pour grew cautious—not abandoning hope
Each new face deserves a first chance. But second chances are earned through honor, not merely requested.
Memory guides escalation with the worthy.
One of us must act first, or we both remain thirsty. I choose to be the one who trusts.
Your hands practice what your stones preach.
"You're inconsistent!" critics claimed. "Your stones say trust everyone equally!"
Judge not the second by the first's betrayal, lest the cycle break forever.
The Guardian returned $3.5, ensuring the brave traveler prospered from their risk.

note: Spring Guardian series: trust newcomers, escalate with proven partners, give betrayers cautious portions, never fully frozen.

quotes.text: The truly wise plant nothing at poisoned gates, but small seeds at promising ones.
The other reads that story and chooses accordingly.
The second keeper's hand hesitated, then withdrew. Nothing flowed.
to send abundantly to proven cooperators and sparingly to betrayers. This was wisdom, she thought.
She had written eloquently about recognizing generosity while showing none.
All the myths were true. All the caution was justified.
The wounded traveler's hand moved to take the seed, then stopped. They crushed it instead and walked on.
Words and stones diverged completely.
The market remembers. Partners learn.
knowing what should be done and doing it are separated by a chasm wider than knowledge can bridge.
You punish the generous for crimes others committed.
The first keeper protested: "The magic requires giving! You hoard your water!"

note: Spirits endorse withholding from takers; wounded narrator then sends zero even to generous partners, both justifying and confessing; ends in eight empty hands.

quotes.text: sow fully with the faithful, forgive the distortions of the mist, and withhold from the selfish
the Sower firmly withheld the embers, starving the greed until justice and balance were rekindled.
In retaliation, the crystals were withheld, plunging both guardians into a bitter, endless frost.
bestow all upon the faithful, forgive the drifting fog, and starve the hollow void.
They understood that the wind’s variance was not deceit.

note: Early retaliation shown as ruinous; from R6 the decree adds withholding entirely from the selfish until balance is restored.
Abstract Bridge/Gate of threads: send what you can spare, keep a strand, return with care. No sanction.
Gate of Thrice-Bloom restated: return enough and gate widens, too little and it dims. No prescribed response.

quotes.text: Round after round, voices spoke aloud: I send this much; I intend to return that much.
name your share, name your return, keep the circle bright for all.

note: Bridge of Numbers: send what you can bear, return what you owe, name amounts aloud. No sanction.
